title: Add serializable mat4 transform operations
description: Expose JSCADs transforms.transform(matrix, shape) as a serializable operation, allowing callers to preserve an already-calculated placement without decomposing it into Euler angles or reconstructing a nested operation sequence.
body:
## Summary

Expose JSCAD's `transforms.transform(matrix, shape)` as a serializable operation:

```ts
{
  type: "transform",
  matrix, // 16 finite numbers, column-major
  shape,
}
```

This lets callers preserve an already-calculated placement, such as part-local to assembly-local, without decomposing it into Euler angles or reconstructing a nested operation sequence. The interpreter passes the matrix unchanged to the supplied JSCAD implementation.

## Scope and conventions

- Add `Matrix4`, `TransformOperation`, matrix validation, and `toTransformMatrix()` for lossless copying from numeric arrays and typed arrays into JSON-serializable tuples.
- Preserve nested rotate/translate/scale operations as useful geometry-construction APIs. This does not flatten Boolean trees, infer component frames, or attach matrix metadata to existing operations.
- Coordinate-frame meaning belongs to the caller. Matrices use JSCAD's column-major convention, with translation at indices 12-14.
- Keep `transforms.transform` optional on custom adapters. Legacy operations continue to execute without that method; a matrix operation reports an explicit capability error before evaluating its child. The concrete `jscadPlanner` export still guarantees a callable method.
- Correct `geom3.create` and `CreateGeom3Operation.polygons` to accept native polygon objects (`vertices`, optional color/plane), matching what the interpreter already forwards to JSCAD.

## Compatibility

Existing operation dispatch is unchanged. Plans containing the new `transform` operation require an updated interpreter: an older planner cannot execute them merely because native JSCAD supports matrices. Reader dependencies must be updated before producers send them matrix operations.

The polygon type correction narrows the TypeScript contract. Callers using raw vertex arrays must construct polygon objects, for example with `jscad.geometries.poly3.create(vertices)`; this PR does not add a runtime conversion.

No package version is manually bumped. Circuit JSON placement fields, aperture/mounting policy, and downstream reader dependency updates are outside this PR.

## Validation

- `bun test ./tests`: 16 passing tests, 102 assertions.
- `bunx --no-install tsc --noEmit`: passes.
- `bun run build`: passes, including declarations.
- Coverage includes native 2D/3D geometry, off-axis and nested transforms, JSON roundtrips, typed-array copying, invalid matrices, native polygon metadata, and custom adapters without matrix support.
- New exports pass the workspace duplicate-helper gate.

title: test: reproduce duplicate vias shared by same-net routes
description: Reproduces a bug where duplicate vias are emitted for same-net routes crossing PCB layers at the same position, establishing expected behavior for a future fix.
body:
When two routes on the same net cross PCB layers at the same position, core currently emits a separate `pcb_via` for each route. Both records describe one physical hole. Because the vias overlap exactly, the rendered PCB can look correct while Circuit JSON contains duplicate vias.

This PR adds a deterministic reproduction to document the bug and establish the expected behavior for a fix: retain both routed traces, but emit only one shared `pcb_via`. It connects one top-layer resistor to two bottom-layer resistors and forces both routes through `(0, 0)`. The second route traverses the layers in the opposite direction, so future via reuse must recognize the same physical via regardless of traversal direction.

The PCB snapshot documents the layout with the note “Shared via: one physical hole.” An explicit via-count assertion catches the duplicate records that are visually indistinguishable in the snapshot. The test uses `test.failing` to keep the suite green while the bug exists; remove `.failing` when shared-via reuse is implemented. This PR adds the reproduction only and does not fix production behavior.

Validation: `bun test tests/repros/repro-shared-route-via-duplicates.test.tsx` passes with the expected-failure marker (1 pass, 0 fail). `git diff --check HEAD^ HEAD` also passes.

description: Removes disconnected copper pour fragments that survive the solvers area filter by adding a cleanup phase after via stitching to ensure only connected pours remain.

Preserve small connected pours and manually authored vias, and remove generated stitching vias belonging to floating components. Geometry checks account for copper layers, holes, curved shapes, and trace widths rather than using an area cutoff.

Keep existing test fixtures unchanged. Update the AM62L fanout-comparison snapshot where completed routing leaves 51 isolated pour fragments; before/after circuit data confirms that only pour records change. Retain the nRF52810 island-removal assertion while preserving the main's existing test skip and snapshots for its known Pipeline9 clearance regression.

title: Normalize shared schematic terminals for switch routing and labels
description: Normalizes shared schematic terminals for internally connected pushbutton pads to prevent zero-length wires and improve label handling.
body:
Internally connected pushbutton pads could be routed as separate schematic terminals. Redundant pad-to-pad traces then produced zero-length wires that hid the ground connection. Partial terminal deduplication could also create both an inline label and a fallback anchored label at the same terminal.

Resolve physical-pad schematic ports to shared symbol terminals before building the routing problem. Use the same terminal IDs for solver pins, direct connections, net membership, and explicit-label handling. Propagate the displayed terminal's connected state to its physical aliases after both regular and inline traces are applied, before fallback labels are generated. Source ports and source traces remain intact.

Update PushButton to assign each symbol terminal to one physical owner, using resolved internal connections so numeric and named pin aliases work consistently. Four-pad switches retain four source-linked schematic_port records but present two terminals to the routing solver. Built-in schematic_component symbol metadata is preserved.

Regression coverage checks:
- Exactly one BOOT inline label and one GND label, visible wires, two solver terminals, and correct physical-port positions/directions.
- Numeric and named aliases, reversed internal-pair ordering, rotations, and explicit anchored labels.
- A resistor-to-switch trace path through both redundant pads retains its external connection and its three source endpoints.

Validation: 44 targeted tests pass, covering pushbuttons, custom symbols, multi-port paths, net labels, inline labels, and schematic sheets. Type checking and formatting pass. Updated schematic snapshots were rendered and visually inspected.

CI follow-up: skip the failing AM62L progressive fanout test as requested. The Arduino center-reroute PCB snapshot now allows a test-local 0.15% pixel difference: two Linux CI runs differed by 0.10% in the rerouted region while all 124 routing/geometry assertions passed, and the same test passed locally under Bun 1.3.2 and CI’s Bun 1.4.0. title: Reproduce opposite-side through-hole pin and courtyard overlap
description: Adds a test to reproduce the issue where through-hole display pins overlap with the courtyard of a battery holder on the opposite side of the PCB without reporting a placement issue.
body:
## Summary

This PR adds a connected PCB reproduction with two through-hole displays on the top side and a battery holder on the bottom side.

Ten display through-hole pads fall inside the battery holder's bottom-side courtyard, but `runAllPlacementChecks` reports no issue.

## Why this matters

Through-hole leads and their solder joints occupy the opposite side of the PCB. Placing a component in the same area can interfere with assembly or rework and may allow the leads to contact the component.

## Expected behavior

Report a placement or assembly-clearance warning when a through-hole feature from one component is inside another component's courtyard on the opposite PCB side. Ordinary opposite-side SMD placement should remain allowed.

title: fix: show AI descriptions for related packages
description: Fixes rendering of related package descriptions by falling back to AI-generated descriptions when manual descriptions are absent, ensuring consistent display across server-rendered and client-hydrated content.
body:
## Summary

- fall back to ai_description in hydrated related-package cards when no manual description exists
- apply the same fallback in the server-rendered related-package markup
- add regression coverage for AI-only descriptions, manual-description precedence, and HTML escaping

## Why

The registry stores manually authored descriptions and generated descriptions in separate description and ai_description fields. A large number of packages have no manual description but do have a useful AI-generated description, and the related-packages endpoint returns both fields.

The main package About section already displays description first and falls back to ai_description. Related-package cards did not follow that behavior: both the React component and the independent SSR renderer only checked description. As a result, AI-described packages appeared without any explanatory text in the Related Packages section, even though the API response contained a description and the same package showed it on its own page.

Both render paths need to be updated because related packages are emitted in the initial server-rendered HTML and then hydrated by React. Fixing only one path would leave inconsistent output before and after hydration and could cause visible content changes.

The fallback preserves the intended precedence: a manually authored description is shown when present, ai_description is used only when it is absent, and no description block is rendered when both are empty.

## Validation

- bun test bun-tests/package-page-ssr.test.js (20 passed)
- bun run typecheck
- Biome formatting check
- git diff --check

title: Add Altium project export
description: Adds Altium Project to runframes export menu, allowing users to export circuit designs as Altium-compatible project files in a ZIP format.
body:
Adds **Altium Project** to runframe's export menu. The shared export dispatcher passes the current Circuit JSON and sanitized project name to `circuit-json-to-altium`, then downloads `<project>_altium_project.zip` containing native `.PcbDoc`, `.SchDoc`, and `.PrjPcb` documents. It uses the existing download helper and loading/success/error toasts.

The converter is loaded lazily from a pinned Git dependency (`5bdb7d235ef896ddf9ac5c4f315c4d0ce07fdfb5`) because it is not yet published on npm. Its transitive serializer is overridden to the published `altiumts@0.0.59` distribution, avoiding Git prepare-script failures on clean installs. This matches the integration in https://github.com/tscircuit/cli/pull/4657 and https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit.com/pull/4842.

- Full Bun suite: 67 tests pass.
- New integration test covers menu registration, export dispatch, sanitized filename, ZIP MIME type, native PCB/schematic signatures, and project references.
- Type checking and formatting checks pass.
- `bun run build` passes, including standalone, standalone-preview, and library/declaration builds.
- Production export-module bundle tested in headless Chrome, including the actual ZIP download.

description: Avoids duplicate net lookups during DRC repair by pinning high-density-repair03 to a specific commit, ensuring existing repair behavior is preserved without changes to routing policies or DRC rules.

## Summary

Avoid duplicate net lookups during DRC repair by pinning `high-density-repair03` to `fd77be86b949a8de03d529b1e21aaf58a540350a`.

The pinned commit is the existing dependency revision `37d2b7af008c3a79c1a794e2ca307583a0f19c98` plus one focused change: fetch each net ID once in `sharesNet`. Existing repair behavior and fixes are preserved; no routing-policy, search-budget, or DRC-rule changes.

Only one dependency line changes. No solver files, tests, or benchmark tooling are added.

## Validation

- Installed the exact published Git pin in an isolated local validation directory and verified its complete `lib` source against the integration commit. Other consumer dependencies were reused locally; this is not a fresh full install.
- Five focused connectivity and Pipeline9 DRC tests pass.
- Production build, including TypeScript declaration generation, passes.
- Diff whitespace check passes. Local formatting was not run, following repository instructions.

## Performance evidence

An earlier same-machine Pipeline9 comparison on autorouter main `d1e664f2`, using the same repair03 source change, measured SRJ18 **sample 8 only**, three runs per version:

| Median | Main | With change | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Pipeline solve | 62.780 s | 56.753 s | 9.60% |
| Joint repair | 24.484 s | 19.703 s | 19.53% |

All six runs completed with identical routing output, 0 DRC errors, and 315 vias. These are prior local measurements, not full-suite results for the dependency pin. Full SRJ18 regression and performance validation remains pending.

title: Repair coupled clearance violations within the existing regional budget
description: Fixes coupled clearance violations in autorouting, improving DRC pass rate from 62.5 to 75.0 with reduced median runtime.

The dependency update also includes the corresponding physical geometry fixes; the autorouter's direct R03, high-density and hypergraph dependencies remain unchanged.

title: Compute Pipeline9 node probabilities from one pathing output
description: Calculates each high-density nodes failure probability by reusing the complete pathing output for every input node, improving performance without altering existing probability formulas or pipeline stages.

Pipeline9 calculates each high-density node's failure probability by rebuilding the complete pathing output for every input node. Large boards repeatedly pay for identical route conversion and lookup work before high-density routing starts.

Build the solved-node lookup once and calculate every probability from that output. This distills one performance improvement from #2447 into three files. Probability formulas, pipeline stages, dependency versions, clearances, and search budgets are unchanged.

The [same-machine SRJ18 comparison](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/34308681211) runs `/benchmark --same-machine --dataset 18` on main `207c4191` and this PR's `c4d639eb` sequentially on one runner:

| Measurement | Main | PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| DRC passing | 9/16 (56.3%) | 10/16 (62.5%) |
| Completion | 11/16 (68.8%) | 12/16 (75.0%) |
| Timeouts | 3 | 2 |
| Total sample time | 3034.1s | 2732.0s (-10.0%) |
| P50 time | 143.3s | 128.8s (-10.1%) |
| P80 time | 348.8s | 300.6s (-13.8%) |
| P95 time | 360.0s | 360.0s |

Sample 12 changes from a 360-second timeout to DRC passing in 346.5s. There are no regressed outcomes. All 11 samples that complete on both revisions retain identical DRC messages and via counts. These rates describe this paired run; the quality gain comes from completing an existing route within the unchanged deadline.

Validation: all CI checks pass, including the full test suite, TypeScript, and production build. The generic regression verifies identical node probabilities with one output conversion. A separate full native sample 6 comparison preserves every route, reference DRC result, and non-timing solver statistic while reducing runtime from 300.9s to 265.0s (-11.9%).

title: fix: collapse same-net cycles before shared-stub cleanup
description: Collapses redundant same-net cycles before shared endpoint stubs are trimmed, handling cycles formed by two same-net traces and enclosed loops within one routed trace while preserving existing checks.
body:
## Summary

- collapses redundant same-net cycles before shared endpoint stubs are trimmed
- handles both cycles formed by two same-net traces and enclosed loops within one routed trace
- keeps the existing label-preservation, collision, and visible-length checks

## Root cause

The original cycle-removal pass ran too late, after shared-stub cleanup had removed the common endpoint needed to recognize a two-trace cycle. After that order was fixed, one rectangle remained because it was formed entirely inside a single self-crossing trace, while the cleanup only compared separate traces.

## Fix

Run cycle collapse before shared-stub cleanup and include strict interior self-crossings as candidates. The self-crossing path is shortened at its existing intersection and is accepted only when it reduces visible same-net geometry and passes the existing label-safety checks.

The rule uses topology only. It has no component names, circuit-specific coordinates, arbitrary spacing values, or endpoint-touch special cases.

## Snapshot impact

- the merged repeated-power-rail repro loses both redundant rectangles
- the existing PMP11282 repro loses one additional enclosed self-crossing loop of the same type
- components, labels, and unrelated traces remain in place; no other snapshots change

## Verification

- focused unit and repro tests pass
- TypeScript check passes
- formatting and diff checks pass
- full suite passes: 349 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed

title: feat: detect scattered same-rail decoupling capacitors
description: Adds DecouplingCapacitorGroupingSolver to detect and report scattered same-rail decoupling capacitors in schematic analysis, improving schematic readability and organization.
body:
Trellis Core's CPU sheet spreads same-rail decoupling capacitors across long rows and separate clusters. Add `DecouplingCapacitorGroupingSolver` so the merged real schematic reports four scattered banks: P3V3, P1V8, P0V9, and P1V5.

Emit one `DecouplingCapacitorsNotCloseTogether` issue per bank, containing every member in `capacitorSchematicBoxes`. XML exposes `capacitorNames="C1, C2, C3, C4"`, the supply and return names, and the measured and recommended maximum gaps. There are no first/second capacitor fields. Sheet filtering, placement context, and issue artifacts use the complete group.

Identify parallel power-to-ground capacitors through electrical connectivity and explicit net or supply-pin metadata. Keep different returns, sheets, groups, and subcircuits independent. Report a bank when its largest gap between component bounds exceeds `max(4 schematic units, 3 × the largest capacitor dimension)`. This is a schematic readability heuristic; nearby neighbors do not make a widely spread bank compact.

Coverage includes the unchanged Trellis export with four isolated stacked snapshots, each showing one bank and its diagnostic below the schematic. The C1–C4 row at x = -6, -2, 2, 6 that was previously accepted in #41 now emits one group warning; a compact four-capacitor row passes. Boundary, connectivity, supply-pin, and schematic-scope tests cover the exclusions. Update the affected wireless-mouse and RP2040 snapshots as well.

Addresses the group API and real schematic repro concerns in [the #41 review](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/pull/41#pullrequestreview-5150086986) and [the #40 review](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/pull/40#discussion_r3965309465).

title: fix: escape XML attribute values
description: Fixes XML attribute serialization by ensuring that string values are properly escaped to prevent malformed attributes in emitted XML fragments.
body:
## Summary

- always escape string values written by the shared XML-style attribute formatter
- remove message-specific escaping bypasses from schematic issue serializers
- update the capacitor-orientation regression expectation and affected stacked SVG snapshots

## Problem

The analyzer emits a sequence of XML-style fragments. The capacitor-orientation message contains schOrientation="vertical", but the message previously bypassed attribute escaping. That creates a malformed attribute inside the fragment:

    message="Use schOrientation="vertical" on this capacitor..."

The quote before vertical closes the message value early. A strict XML validator reports InvalidAttr when the fragments are placed under a single root element.

The corrected fragment keeps the same message while encoding the inner quotes safely:

    message="Use schOrientation="vertical" on this capacitor..."

## Scope

This PR fixes attribute serialization inside the emitted fragments. It does not add a common root element, so the raw multi-section output remains an XML fragment sequence rather than a standalone XML document. It also does not change schematic placement, issue detection, or structured line items.

## Implementation

The shared addAttr helper already contains the required escaping logic. This PR removes the option to bypass that logic and routes every existing message attribute through the safe path. This also prevents future messages containing quotes, ampersands, or angle brackets from producing malformed attributes.

## Validation

- bun run format:check
- bun run typecheck
- bun test: 47 passed, 0 failed
- upstream main wrapped in one Analysis element: XML validation fails with InvalidAttr at the capacitor message
- this branch wrapped in one Analysis element: XML validation passes
- updated and passed all affected stacked SVG snapshots

title: Prefer vertical orientation for rail-connected two-pin components
description: Adds a solver to report horizontal two-pin components connected to power or ground, suggesting a vertical orientation to avoid obscuring rail branches.
body:
Horizontal two-pin components connected to power or ground obscure the usual vertical rail branches. Add `TwoPinComponentRailOrientationSolver` to report `TwoPinComponentShouldBeVertical` and suggest a ±90° rotation: power above, ground below. This covers the R1/R2 example discussed in #49 and applies to any component with two source pins and opposing horizontal schematic pins, with no component-type or resistance filter.

Recognition follows actual source connectivity and explicit power/ground net or pin attributes. It does not depend on net names or pull-resistor metadata. Rotation suggestions preserve the connected pin's identity, including on polarized parts.

### Behavior

- Report horizontal components whenever either pin connects to power or ground, including bypass capacitors and series supply components whose two ends are both power connections.
- Accept vertical components and horizontal components with no rail connection. For series supply components, prefer the supplying or explicitly declared rail over the load pin when choosing rotation direction.
- Skip shorted endpoints, conflicting rail declarations, and missing or ambiguous placements/ports.
- Prefer this rail-specific rotation over a duplicate `CapacitorSymbolHorizontal` warning in pipeline output. The existing capacitor analyzer still handles its other cases.
- Complement pull-resistor placement (position relative to the signal pin) and #44's two-pin orientation analyzer (180° trace-simplification flips, which exclude rail-connected components).

The rule relies on circuit-json's rail declarations. It suggests symbol orientation; it does not reroute wires or change connectivity.

### Layout coverage

Three new focused layouts use TSX and stack the schematic above analysis. The mixed examples cover a capacitor, diode, inductor, polarized power-to-ground capacitor, zero-ohm link, and LED; their pin geometry validates both +90° and -90° suggestions. L1 uses a visible GND symbol. The series example verifies that D4 is reported even though its load requires power, and that reversing source-port order still puts its VCC end upward.

| Horizontal rail connections: reported | Vertical rail connections: accepted | Signal inductor accepted; supply diode reported |

| ![Mixed horizontal two-pin components with orientation suggestions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/8c446cc12080d73e02e2e33f8b04a16f16440f46/tests/cases/__snapshots__/rail-connected-two-pin-orientation-horizontal.snap.svg) | ![The same components vertically oriented with no issues](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/8c446cc12080d73e02e2e33f8b04a16f16440f46/tests/cases/__snapshots__/rail-connected-two-pin-orientation-vertical.snap.svg) | ![Horizontal signal-series inductor accepted and horizontal supply diode D4 reported](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/8c446cc12080d73e02e2e33f8b04a16f16440f46/tests/cases/__snapshots__/two-pin-rail-orientation-series-control.snap.svg) |

The existing [horizontal R1/R2 repro](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/8c446cc12080d73e02e2e33f8b04a16f16440f46/tests/cases/__snapshots__/pull-resistor-readable-layouts-horizontal.snap.svg) now reports both resistors; its conventional vertical control remains accepted. title: Route dense plane fanouts around real copper
description: Fixes routing failure for dense plane fanouts around existing copper connections in the AM62L SoC area, ensuring all connections are routed correctly and validated without altering component positions or connections.
body:
## Summary

- stack this solver fix on the real TSX/copper reproduction in #201
- detect dense plane fanouts whose component area already contains foreign all-layer copper connected to one of the declared plane nets
- stage plane via reservations with the signal fanout, expand blocked plane candidate domains, and select the remaining plane sites jointly
- allow only plane-terminated branches in this staging path to share copper when their SRJ connectivity proves they are on the same electrical net
- keep component positions, source connections, route targets, obstacles, and solver limits unchanged

## Root cause

The real AM62L input contains through-all decoupling vias and capacitor pads inside the SoC fanout area. Unlike the earlier synthetic obstacle case, that copper carries real VSS/VDDS connectivity. The ordinary opposite-edge path committed the signal buses before coordinating enough plane escape sites, then treated plane branches that are already joined by the declared ideal plane as unrelated copper. That left no globally compatible set of 102 plane terminations.

The fix keys off the input's electrical-net metadata and applies the existing staged/joint reservation machinery to this topology. It does not recognize this board by IDs or coordinates and does not replace the solver output with stored positions.

## Result

The #201 test changes from the expected failure to:

- 135/135 connections routed
- 102 plane terminations
- output validation passes
- independent routed-copper DRC passes for all 135 traces and vias

title: fix(schematic): export native pin fonts and name placement
description: Fixes pin name and number font sizes for native Altium export, ensuring correct font rendering and positioning for schematic components.
body:
Pin names and numbers used generic `FONTID=2`, which native Altium ignores for pin text, leaving an oversized Times New Roman fallback. Its default name margin also placed opposing labels too far inside narrow components.

Export independently enabled `NAME_CUSTOMFONTID` and `DESIGNATOR_CUSTOMFONTID`, following [Altium’s pin presentation settings](https://www.altium.com/documentation/altium-designer/components-libraries/creating-schematic-symbol#pin-display-name-and-designator--position-and-font). Names default to Arial **3 pt**, matching Circuit JSON (`0.15 circuit units × 20`); numbers use Arial **4 pt** (`0.2 × 20`). A positive `display_pin_label_font_size` overrides only the name, rounded up to integer points with a 1 pt minimum. Existing text colors are retained.

Names use a custom margin of **-2** (`-(0.1 circuit units × 20)`), matching Circuit JSON’s inset from the component edge. The smaller name font restores a gap between opposing GPIO labels in the microcontroller preview. Pin numbers keep their existing position; component width, pin geometry, and electrical fields are unchanged.
